svg.title: A paired tail witnesses noncentral modular time
svg.desc: The matrix unit e12 tensor e21 maps the basis vector e2 tensor e1 to e1 tensor e2. Both have product-state mass lambda divided by the square of one plus lambda. Their joint modular frequencies cancel, while action on the first tensor factor alone multiplies the matrix unit by exp(i p log lambda). The sharp norm is square root of two lambda divided by one plus lambda.

g.text: h = diag(λ, 1)/(1 + λ), Ω = ω ⊗ ω, xₙ = e₁₂ at site n ⊗ e₂₁ at site n
Joint modular action: the phases cancel
(σₜ ⊗ σₜ)(xₙ) = exp(i t log λ) exp(−i t log λ) xₙ = xₙ
The tail centralizes Ω and eventually commutes with every fixed local algebra.
First factor only: one phase remains
α = σₚ ⊗ id, αᵏ(xₙ) = exp(i k p log λ) xₙ
For T = 2π/(−log λ), this phase equals 1 exactly when k p/T is an integer.
‖αᵏ(xₙ) − xₙ‖Ω♯ = |exp(i k p log λ) − 1| √(2λ)/(1 + λ)
If p/T is irrational, the displayed norm is positive for every nonzero integer k.
Here σₜ denotes the modular action of ω. Proofs and arbitrary-state transport: Sections 3–5.
